label: input token n during the original phase
explanation: Fires on every input of the letter n while the original sequence is being read (t < L), and on essentially nothing else: no other token, never at the delimiter, and only about 0.1% of activations (105 steps) fall in the copy phase, when n is fed back as an input. Magnitude is highest when n is the first token (t=0, at max activation), about 0.8-0.9 of max at later positions on a first occurrence, and much weaker (about 0.2-0.6) on repeat occurrences of n. In examples, repeats late in the sequence are the weakest. Restricting to first occurrences drops recall to 0.91, so repeats are a real but weak part of the feature.

issues: Minor: the explanation gives repeat occurrences of n as about 0.2-0.6 of max, but adjacent repeats can be stronger. Dev examples show 0.87, 0.77 and 0.72 (e.g. 'n n 0 n n ...'), and one first occurrence was only 0.46. Magnitude falls with position and with repetition, but the bands are not as clean as stated.

The copy-phase activations (109 test steps, about 0.0% of activation mass) are all very weak (0.00-0.05 of max). They appear at step L+1 in L=3 sequences that start with n, when n is fed back. Precision there is only 0.24 (n_predicted 450), so this is weak noise, not a real part of the feature. The 'about 0.1% in copy phase' claim is accurate.

Verified: 0 false positives on the test split (precision 1.000, recall 0.999, F1 0.9995, mass recall 1.000). Never fires at the delimiter, no other input token is active, activation mass by t falls from 0.20 at t=0, and restricting to first occurrences gives recall 0.907 (mass recall 0.928), as claimed. Repeats alone: recall 0.092, precision 1.0.
